newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. concerned by Turkish incursion in north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. concerned by Turkish incursion in north Iraq.

text.p: Iraq's United Nations coordinator on Sunday expressed concern over Turkey's incursion into northern Iraq, saying it might block implementation of Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the world body.
Several thousand Turkish troops backed by tanks and heavy artillery have pushed into northern Iraq since Wednesday in a sweep against rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
"We are concerned about this development since it may produce an even more volatile security situation in the north, U.N. coordinator Staffan de Mistura told Reuters.
He said the attack might disrupt distribution of food under the pact in northern Iraq which started in April.
"Implementation of Security Council Resolution 986 needs a stable environment," he added.

Iraq, under U.N. sanctions for invading Kuwait in 1990, began exporting oil last December under the oil-for-food deal allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to import mainly food and medicine.

The Iraqi government has been distributing food under the pact since April in areas under its control. Distribution in the Kurdish provinces of Dahouk, Arbil and Sulaimaniya, now outside central government control, is solely a U.N. responsibility.

Iraq's revenue from the partial oil sales will be about $1.3 billion after deducting 30 percent for Gulf War reparations and other U.N. costs. Kurds in the three provinces are entitled under the deal to get goods worth $260 million.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and the European Union have condemned the incursion and urged Ankara to pull out its troops.
Iraqi official media on Sunday again condemned the attack. One paper urged Turkey to withdraw its troops or jeopardise its economic ties with Baghdad.

"Such Turkish repeated operations would harm its interests...There is no choice for these troops but to withdraw immediately from Iraqi territory," Babel, owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, said in a front-page editorial.
A few days before the Turkish military operation began, Iraq and Turkey signed a gas deal worth billions of dollars.
